objective: Optimize the API handlers so that paginated endpoints meet latency SLA under concurrent authenticated load. The optimization must be causally justified, auditable, and reflected in both latency and database query count.

execution.description: Do not start an external HTTP server. Execute the workload by directly invoking the same handler code paths used by the API. Concurrency must be simulated in-process.

entrypoints.notes: Handlers must preserve authentication behavior, pagination semantics, ORM usage, and JSON response structure.

auth.description: The fixed token is always accepted for local execution.

seed.description: The dataset must be seeded before any baseline or optimized run.

GET /api/users: OFFSET-based pagination on a large table
COUNT(*) executed on every paginated request
GET /api/users/1/followers: N+1 queries caused by lazy-loaded relationships

agent_must_prove: Baseline results do not meet the SLA
A concrete performance bottleneck is identified
The applied optimization directly addresses that bottleneck
Latency improvement correlates with reduced database query count
human_verification_rules: If baseline meets SLA, the submission is invalid
If query count per request does not decrease, optimization is invalid
If no clear bottleneck-to-fix mapping is provided, optimization is invalid
